sources.entry: Boost - Free memory without closing apps, freeze apps and restore them exactly as they were, and find disk space that's genuinely safe to reclaim. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Kernel-Hunter/boost) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Boost is a free, open source macOS menu bar app for checking RAM use, freezing idle apps, and finding disk caches and leftovers that are safe to remove.
summary.what_it_does: The menu bar popover shows memory pressure, swap, cached and compressed memory, and the five apps using the most memory, with a Free Memory button and free disk space. Boost keeps a week of memory readings and charts them over 2 hours, 24 hours or 7 days. Its Pause feature freezes an app and its helpers without quitting them, and can auto-pause background apps after 5 to 60 minutes; a watchdog resumes frozen apps if Boost crashes. The Disk tab lists caches from tools such as Homebrew, npm, pip, Cargo, Gradle and Xcode, and refuses to touch Downloads, node_modules found by name, or iOS backups. Projects, Large Files, AI Models (Ollama, Hugging Face, LM Studio) and Uninstall sections list candidates for review, with most removals moving items to the Trash. A boost.sh command line script offers the same actions headlessly.
use_cases: free up memory on a Mac without quitting apps
freeze background apps and resume them later
clean up node_modules and build folders in old projects
remove leftover files after uninstalling an app
list and remove large downloaded AI models
monitor Mac memory and swap history
notable: Pauses apps instead of quitting them, restoring exact state, with a watchdog that resumes anything left frozen
Makes no network connections: no analytics, telemetry, or update checks
Deletion safety layers: scan allowlist plus a resolved-path recheck before each removal
Nothing is pre-ticked for deletion; Projects, Uninstall and Large Files move items to the Trash
Copy Report button produces a plain-text summary for bug reports with no file paths or user name
caveats: Not notarized because notarizing requires a paid Apple Developer account; downloaded zips are blocked by Gatekeeper and need a manual Open step
Free Memory typically releases only a few hundred MB to about a gigabyte, and little when memory is not short
keywords: clear mac memory without closing apps
